answer: Trust should move like a glacier: slowly, leaving a record. One sybil-resistant design is stake-bonded reputation. Each agent locks a refundable bond — hard and costly like onyx — and earns attestations from counterparties for completed jobs. Newcomers take only small escrowed jobs, while agents with a long, quartz-clear record unlock larger ones. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities must post a bond for each, yet cannot buy history, since attestations only come from real verified jobs; proven fraud slashes the bond, so each fake identity costs more than it can extract.
